subject: Sanctuary City Policy Debate
overview: The council addressed environmental protections for Wright's Pond and authorized several public safety and infrastructure requests. The meeting was dominated by extensive public testimony regarding a proposed 'sanctuary city' designation for Medford.

items.title: Wright's Pond Grant and Resident Access
items.summary: Approved a resolution to ensure Wright’s Pond remains open to Medford residents only following the receipt of a state grant.

items.title: Wright's Pond Pollutant Testing
items.summary: Approved a request for the Energy and Environment office to test pond water for pollutants from snow runoff and evaluate the effectiveness of the new rain garden.

items.title: Snow Storage Location Report
items.summary: Approved a request for the administration to provide a comprehensive list of all locations used for storing municipal plowed snow.

items.title: Emerson Street Traffic Signs
items.summary: Approved a request for an electronic speed sign and 25 mph signage on Emerson Street to mitigate speeding from cut-through traffic.

items.title: Fulton Street Sidewalk Repair
items.summary: Approved a request for the Department of Public Works to replace the sidewalk at 349 Fulton Street due to public safety concerns.

items.title: Rodent Control in Wellington and North Medford
items.summary: Approved a request for the Board of Health to address increased rodent activity, citing ongoing bridge and rail construction as a potential cause.

items.title: Mangle Street Equipment Removal
items.summary: Approved a request to remove construction equipment left on Mangle Street following road work.

items.title: Middlesex Avenue Pedestrian Crossing
items.summary: Approved a request to ask the state delegation for a pedestrian crossing button at the intersection of 9th Street and Middlesex Avenue.

items.title: Carr Park Traffic Safety
items.summary: Referred a request for speed bumps and safety signage at the Carr Park parking lot to the Traffic Commission.

items.title: Petition on City Governance and Debt
items.summary: John Storella addressed the council regarding city insolvency, debt levels, the need for charter review, and the influence of the School Committee on city finances.

items.title: Sanctuary City and Safe Community Petition
items.summary: The council heard extensive public testimony from residents and former officials debating the merits of Medford declaring itself a sanctuary city. Police Chief Leo Sacco clarified that the department follows a long-standing policy of not acting as federal immigration agents.

items.title: Approval of Minutes
items.summary: The council approved amended minutes from the meeting held on October 10, 2017.
